notes: The numeral phrase is compressed: Hebrew writes about ... men twice and the ASV once, so the second kaph and the first 'ish go unrepresented under rules 22 and 25, the rendered occurrences read tail-to-tail.
The but of but let ... is added because the second jussive clause is juxtaposed with no conjunction in it (rule 14, closing sentences).
The restrictive but of are but few is kept with me'at; marking it added was the competing reading and is named in that unit's note.
